A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DATAMIND work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison; retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations in Table 1 and experiments on trajectory filtering, training stability, and cold-start training in Figures 3–6.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds training ablations, evaluator comparisons, additional model and benchmark evaluations, and a contamination analysis.

M1.justification: The synthesis pipeline, trajectory filtering, hybrid SFT–DAPO objective, rewards, and rollout procedure remain unchanged in Sections 3–4. The prompt appendix is unchanged after renumbering. The Llama experiment applies the existing procedure without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Appendix G.3 adds QRData evaluation, extending the retained tabular-analysis coverage to additional challenging causal-reasoning questions requiring domain knowledge. DABench, TableBench, and BIRD remain. The unexplained DATAMIND-14K reference in Appendix G.1 does not establish a distinct training corpus.

E2.justification: Data Interpreter changes from cited related work to an evaluated comparator across four backbones on DABench and TableBench (Table 5). Table 2 also introduces a direct comparison with pure SFT, zero-RL, and SFT-then-RL. These substantially expand the comparisons beyond the unchanged Table 1 comparator set.

E3.justification: The reported RL batch and minibatch sizes change from 16/2 to 32/4; this does not establish that the retained results were rerun. New experiments introduce training-data subsets, a Llama-3.1-8B backbone, 14B cold-start tests, external Qwen-2.5-72B judging, and Rouge-L evaluation of descriptive TableBench tasks.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's filtering and training-stability analyses, v2 tests data-volume scaling, training-strategy contributions, and dependence on evaluator choice and metric (Section 5.3 and Appendix G.4). It also adds header-overlap contamination analysis and extends the cold-start study from 7B to 14B.

E5.justification: Both versions retain three evaluation trials and the same pass@1/pass@3 aggregation. V2 newly discloses 'many trials' for zero-RL and SFT-then-RL, with validation-based checkpoint selection, and introduces Pearson correlation for judge agreement. Exact training-run counts, seeds, and uncertainty intervals are not supplied.

E6.justification: Table 1 is unchanged, including average pass@1 scores of 68.10% and 71.16%. Added results include zero-RL at 58.03% and SFT-then-RL at 63.42% average pass@1, Llama-8B at 65.56%, and DATAMIND-14B on QRData at 62.04%/77.62% pass@1/pass@3. Further additions report Data Interpreter, scaling, evaluator-agreement, and header-overlap findings.

T1.justification: The task and trajectory definitions and Equations 1–8 are retained. The added scaling, evaluator, and contamination analyses introduce no new theoretical propositions, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same core contributions: the DATAMIND pipeline, DATAMIND-12K, the 7B/14B agents, and their benchmark-superiority claims. Additional experiments support these claims without substantively redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly attributes most performance gains to training data and adds interpretations concerning evaluator reliability, transfer across model families, scaffolding, and QRData's knowledge demands. It adds a tabular-data/text-only limitation and removes v1's conjecture about a cold-start strength beyond which RL provides no improvement. Appendix H also newly claims absence of contamination from header overlap.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents a ten-round interaction limit, eight 80GB A100 GPUs, training within two days, and baseline input-format reproduction details. The abstract changes the resource-release statement to completed release, but the reproducibility statement still promises future release, leaving availability internally inconsistent.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Gandhi et al., OctoThinker, Llama 3.1, and DataWiseAgent to contextualize model selection and reproduction findings. Appendix G.2 strengthens the argument for agent training over scaffolding, while Section 6 and the detailed related-work appendix remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. V2 inserts an ablation subsection and two experimental appendices, renumbers Analysis and the prompt appendix, adds acknowledgments, and updates the publication header. These are localized structural changes rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: V2 adds data-volume and judge-agreement plots and six comparison or analysis tables. It expands the cold-start plot with 14B series, updates Figure 1's display and caption, and relocates retained figures and tables. This substantially expands the visual presentation of evidence.

improvement.justification: V1 lacked direct full-benchmark training-strategy controls and an external check of its training/evaluation judge. V2 supplies both (Table 2 and Figure 5), alongside cross-family and QRData evaluations, substantially strengthening support for the training and generalization claims. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses, including the undefined DATAMIND-14K reference, stale Qwen-only limitation, and overstrong no-contamination conclusion from header overlap.
